text:
Jess: heads-up — ran a low-sample profiling pass on host-side tokenization + grpc framing for the internal batch router. saw a ~12% p99 regression after the kernel selection change.
Anya: ugh, can you paste the flame output or toplines?
Jess: pasted a trimmed trace: ```hotspots: host_parse: 41%\nkv_lookup: 12%\ngrpc_writev: 9%\ntokenize: 7%\nkernel_selector: 5%``` looks like host_parse + kv interactions increased.
Sam: @jess did you use the new batching heuristic? small-batch fast-path might be hitting a different kernel path.
Jess: yes — tested with batch_hint=auto and kernel preference=latency-first. switching to throughput-first drops host_parse by ~4% in the trace (quick local).
Lee: interesting — could be the kernel change altered pad/unpack ordering, causing extra copies before kvcache hits.
Anya: any evidence of extra copies? trace samples around host_parse show memcpy calls in the preparse stage.
Jess: snippet: ```#0 host_preparse_memcpy 0x7ff\n#1 token_shim_unpack 0x3a\n#2 kv_cache_lookup 0x1f``` so memcpy is happening pre-kv lookup.
Sam: that suggests we're tokenizing to a temp buffer instead of in-place. maybe grpc framing expects contiguous chunks now and we allocate.
Anya: does the grpc writev change affect this? infra-bot: deploy-benchbot finished: summary: grpc_writev latency +1.1ms median under microburst, writev coalescing disabled in new kernel.
Lee: okay, so two levers: kernel selection policy and writev/coalesce behavior. We should test combinations: (latency-first/throughput-first) x (writev coalesce on/off).
Jess: plan: run 1) reproduce on perf cluster with 1000 qps synthetic, trace collection 2) iterate toggles 3) capture kvcache hit-rate and host-parse memallocs. I'll post results by EOD.
Sam: also add a runtime experiment to avoid making a contiguous copy if kvcache lookup is cheap; only make copy on miss. cheap guard.
Anya: +1. Also add a quick unit to assert no unexpected memcpy in hot path (flame) to catch regressions.
Lee: I'll instrument an alloc counter on the preparse buffer and create a small opt-in knob. could be a hot fix.
Jess: thanks team. if anyone wants to pair on the perf cluster run ping me. :thumbsup:
